name: Starter: Serbian
about: Serbian word order and cases in real, everyday sentences.

words.кућа: house, home (код куће: at home; кући: home)
words.звати се: to be called (како се зовеш: what's your name)
words.свиђати се: to please (свиђа ми се: I like it)

добар-дан.about: The everyday polite greeting, literally good day.

извините.about: To get someone's attention or say sorry: polite to one person, or to more than one; one friend gets Извини.

concept.line: The verb's ending marks the person: (ја) живим, (ти) живиш, (он, она) живи, (ми) живимо, (ви) живите, (они) живе.
A Serbian verb marks the person, so ја (I), ти (you), он, она (he, she) and ми (we) are usually left out when it's clear who: Живим у малом стану (I live in a small apartment).

words.means: си = you are; јеси = are you; нисам = I am not

concept.line: Short unstressed words like сам, си, је, се, ми, ти, нас and те follow the first word or phrase: Јуче сам био код куће; Свиђа ми се овај филм; Учитељ сам.

words.means: имам = I have; имаш = you have

concept.line: Serbian nouns are masculine (often a consonant: стан), feminine (often -а: кухиња) or neuter (often -о or -е: млеко), and the words with them match: мој брат, моја мама.

words.means: говориш = you speak; говорим = I speak
разумем = I understand; разумеш = you understand

concept.line: The accusative marks direct objects: a feminine singular -а often becomes -у (кафа, кафу), and a masculine singular person or animal usually takes the genitive's form (видим брата); it also follows у or на for where you're going and у for days: у продавницу, на плажу, у суботу.

words.means: живим = I live; живиш = you live; живи = lives
идем = I go; идеш = you go; иде = goes

concept.line: A yes/no question starts with да ли, or puts ли after the verb (Да ли говориш енглески?
